sessions.brainstorm:
"What words can you think of with tract in them?" 20 sec, turn and tell, then cold call four pairs.
EXPECT: tractor, subtract, attract, extract.
CLARIFY: track, like a running track, is not a tract word - it has no t at the end. Listen for the whole tract.

words_to_read_new.meaning: TRACT means pull + -or means a thing that: a machine that pulls
TRACT means pull + -ion means the act of: the act of pulling, the grip that lets a wheel pull
ex- means out + TRACT means pull: to pull out
sub- means under + TRACT means pull: to take away, to pull out from under
con- means together + TRACT means pull: to pull together
re- means back + TRACT means pull: to pull back
sub- means under + TRACT means pull + -ion means the act of: the act of taking away
at- means toward + TRACT means pull: to pull toward
dis- means away + TRACT means pull: to pull your attention away

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: the card lists subtraction; subtract is its simpler sibling (sub- + tract, nothing untaught), the verb students use in every maths lesson, and the base Tuesday's spelling builds on.
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: subtract, to take (one number or quantity) from another; deduct.

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: the card lists retraction; retract is its simpler sibling (re- back + tract pull) and the picturable one - a cat retracts its claws.
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: retract, to draw back or in.

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: the card lists attraction; attract is its simpler sibling, and the persuasive writing unit needs it (attract voters, attract customers).
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: attract, to draw by a physical force; to draw by appeal to the emotions or senses.

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: the card lists distraction; distract is its simpler sibling, one part shorter, and an everyday classroom word.
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: distract, to draw away or divert, as the mind or attention.

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
SAY: "Learn tract once and you can read a whole family of words about pulling."
READ each word as it appears, say what it means, then link tract to the card meaning: pull.
tractor - TRACT means pull + or means a thing that: a machine that pulls. A tractor pulls the plough across the paddock.
traction - TRACT + ion means the act of: the grip that lets a wheel pull. Footy boots give you traction on wet grass.
extract - ex means out + TRACT means pull: to pull out. The dentist had to extract my wobbly tooth.
subtract - sub means under + TRACT: to pull out from under, to take away. Subtract 10 from 50 and you get 40.
contract - con means together + TRACT: to pull together. Muscles contract to lift your arm. A contract is a deal that pulls two people together.
retract - re means back + TRACT: to pull back. A cat can retract its claws.
subtraction - sub + TRACT + ion: the act of taking away. A 25% discount is a subtraction from the price.
attract - at means toward + TRACT: to pull toward. A good poster will attract people to your stall.
distract - dis means away + TRACT: to pull your attention away. Do not let your phone distract you from homework.

keyword_sentence.title: Pick your own tract word
keyword_sentence.rule: Two jobs in your OG book
keyword_sentence.example:
1. Your own tract word for pull. Star it.
2. Write one sentence that shows what it means.
items: My word: **tractor** - The **tractor** pulled a trailer full of hay.
keyword_sentence.footer: Check: does it make the meaning clear?
keyword_sentence.notes:
1. SAY: "The card keyword is detract. De means away, tract means pull: to pull away from something. Litter can detract from a beautiful beach."
2. SAY: "If another tract word helps YOU remember pull, pick that one, like tractor. Write it at the bottom of the page and star it."
3. SAY: "Then write one sentence with your word, so a reader can tell what it means." TIME: 3 min, then cold call two students to read theirs.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one sentence that uses two tract words and still makes sense.
HELP: give a stem, "The tractor pulled..." or "Our poster will attract...", and let them finish it.
---
ANSWERS: open - e.g. Mine: tractor. The tractor pulled a trailer full of hay. EXTENSION: e.g. The noisy tractor will distract us from our subtraction.

matrix.title: Build tract words
matrix.rule: Build real words. Write each one and what it means.
matrix.notes:
1. SAY: "tract is in the middle. Join a part from the left, the right, or both, and build a real word. Write the word and what it means."
2. MODEL: say "ex plus tract: extract, to pull out", and write it on the class board.
3. TIME: 4 min. CIRCULATE: to a stuck student say, "Start with tract. Put sub in front. What does subtract mean?"
4. ASK: "Read me your longest word and what it means." Cold call two students. EXPECT: retractable, able to be pulled back, like a pen; attractive, relating to pulling people toward it.
TRAP: a made-up word that sounds right, like subtractable. Fix: ask, would you read that in a newspaper? Student builds a real one.
EXTENSION: Longest word hunt - build the longest real word you can and write its parts.
HELP: give three starters, extract, subtract, contract, and ask for one ending on each.
---
ANSWERS: extract, subtract, contract, retract, attract; add -ion for the act of: extraction, subtraction, contraction, retraction, attraction, traction.
Also: tractor, contractor (a thing or one that); attractive (relating to); retractable (able to be pulled back); extracted, subtracted, contracted, attracted.
EXTENSION: e.g. retractable = re + tract + able; attractions = at + tract + ion + s.

rounds.title: Break the word into its parts
rounds.rule: Write only the parts in the boxes. tract is done for you.

round.notes:
1. SAY: "We just built words. Now we do the opposite. I show a whole word, you write its parts in boxes."
2. MODEL: point at subtraction. SAY: "I find tract first. In front is sub. Behind is ion. Three parts, three boxes: sub, tract, ion."
3. SAY: "Three words, one at a time. Write only the parts in your OG book, then I click."
EXTENSION: Beat the number - break 5 more tract words from the matrix into parts in 2 minutes.
HELP: underline tract in each word first, then split what is left on each side.
---
ANSWERS: 1. re + tract + able  2. con + tract + or  3. ex + tract + ed. EXTENSION: e.g. at + tract + ive, re + tract + ion, ex + tract + ion.

round.why: able to be pulled back, like a pen
round.notes:
ANSWER: re + tract + able.
1. ASK: "Write the parts of retractable." 20 sec. Cue: "Pens down when you are done."
2. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> cover the able with your hand and ask what is left, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Re means back, able means able to. A retractable pen can be pulled back in."
TRAP: splitting it retr + actable. Fix: find tract first, student rewrites the parts around it.

round.why: one who signs a deal to do a job
round.notes:
ANSWER: con + tract + or.
1. ASK: "Write the parts of contractor." 20 sec. Cue: "Pens down when you are done."
2. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> point at tract and ask what is in front of it and what is behind it, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Con means together, or means one who. A contractor signs a contract to do a job, like building our new gym."
TRAP: writing contracter with er. Fix: this word ends in -or, like tractor; student swaps the e for o.

ANSWER: ex + tract + ed.
1. ASK: "Write the parts of extracted." 20 sec. Cue: "Pens down when you are done."
2. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> cover the ed and ask what is left, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Ex plus tract plus ed. Pulled out, and ed tells us it already happened."
TRAP: leaving off the ed box. Fix: count the boxes on the slide, student adds the third part.

rounds.title: Which tract word is it?
rounds.rule: Write the tract word that matches. Whiteboards.

round.prompt:
One done for you:
a machine that pulls a plough
round.notes:
1. SAY: "Now the other way round. I read what the word means, you write the word."
2. MODEL: "A machine that pulls. Pull is tract, a thing that is or. Tractor."
3. SAY: "Four more. Write it on your whiteboard. Write it... chin it... show me."

round.prompt:
to pull out a tooth
that is wobbly or sore
round.notes:
ANSWER: extract.
1. ASK: "Write the tract word." 15 sec. Cue: "Write it... chin it... show me."
2. SCAN the boards. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> ask what part means out, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after boards are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Ex means out. Extract."
TRAP: writing extrack. Fix: say tract slowly, student ends it with ct.

round.prompt:
to take one number
away from another
round.notes:
ANSWER: subtract.
1. ASK: "Write the tract word." 15 sec. Cue: "Write it... chin it... show me."
2. SCAN the boards. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> write 50 - 10 on the class board and ask what we do, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after boards are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Sub plus tract. Subtract, to take away."
TRAP: writing subtraction. Fix: the meaning says to take, something you do; student drops the ion.

round.prompt:
a written deal that
two people sign
round.notes:
ANSWER: contract.
1. ASK: "Write the tract word." 15 sec. Cue: "Write it... chin it... show me."
2. SCAN the boards. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> ask what an entrepreneur signs with a shark, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after boards are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Con means together. A contract pulls two people together in one deal."
TRAP: writing contact. Fix: listen for the r, con-tract; student adds it.

round.prompt:
to pull people toward you,
like a magnet
round.notes:
ANSWER: attract.
1. ASK: "Write the tract word." 15 sec. Cue: "Write it... chin it... show me."
2. SCAN the boards. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> point back at Monday's magnet and ask what it does, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after boards are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. At means toward. Attract, to pull toward, like our magnet."
TRAP: writing atract with one t. Fix: at plus tract, two t's; student adds the t.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one sentence that uses attract and subtract and makes sense. e.g. Our stall will attract shoppers if we subtract $5 from every price.
---
ANSWERS: tractor (worked), extract, subtract, contract, attract.

intro.title: Noun, verb or adjective?
intro.rule: Read the sentence. What job does the bold word do?
intro.prompt: Our **attractive** poster pulled people to the stall.
intro.footer: Next: your turn on four suffix cards
intro.notes:
ANSWER: adjective - attractive describes the poster.
1. SAY: "Every word has a job in a sentence. The sentence tells us the job, and the suffix helps."
2. POINT at each choice. SAY: "A noun names a thing or idea. A verb is something you do. An adjective describes a noun."
3. MODEL: read the sentence. SAY: "What sort of poster? An attractive one. Attractive tells us about the poster."
4. SAY: "The doing word is pulled. Poster is the thing. Attractive describes the poster, so it is an adjective." REVEAL on the click.
5. SAY: "Attract is something you do. Add -ive, relating to, and it describes a noun. The suffix changed the job."
TRAP: verb, because attract is an action. Fix: cover the -ive, then show it; student says what the suffix changed.

cards.sentence: The farm machinery pulled the logs out of the creek.
cards.why: machinery is the thing that pulled the logs
cards.notes:
1. READ: "Read the card with me." CHORAL: "-ery means relating to, or place where. The farm machinery pulled the logs out of the creek."
2. ASK: "What job does machinery do in this sentence: noun, verb or adjective?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: noun.
SCAN: split or wrong chorus -> do not click. Ask "What pulled the logs?", then re-ask on three.
3. REVEAL after the choral answer. SAY: "Machinery is the thing that pulled the logs, so it is a noun. -ery words name a thing or a place, so they are nouns."
TRAP: verb, because pulled is an action. Fix: pulled is the verb; ask what pulled the logs, student points at machinery.

cards.sentence: Our coach is a clever tactician who plans every move.
cards.why: tactician is the person who plans every move
cards.notes:
1. READ: "Read the card with me." CHORAL: "-cian means person who. Our coach is a clever tactician who plans every move."
2. ASK: "What job does tactician do in this sentence: noun, verb or adjective?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: noun.
SCAN: split or wrong chorus -> do not click. Ask "Who plans every move?", then re-ask on three.
3. REVEAL after the choral answer. SAY: "A tactician is the person who plans every move, so it is a noun. -cian means person who, so -cian words name people. They are nouns."
TRAP: adjective, because clever sits next to it. Fix: clever describes the tactician; ask who plans, student says tactician.

cards.sentence: Two umpires will officiate at our footy final.
cards.why: officiate is what the umpires will do
cards.notes:
1. READ: "Read the card with me." CHORAL: "-ciate means to make. Two umpires will officiate at our footy final."
2. ASK: "What job does officiate do in this sentence: noun, verb or adjective?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: verb.
SCAN: split or wrong chorus -> do not click. Ask "What will the umpires do?", then re-ask on three.
3. REVEAL after the choral answer. SAY: "Officiate is what the umpires will do, so it is a verb. -ciate means to make, and making is something you do, so -ciate words are usually verbs."
TRAP: noun, because umpires are people. Fix: umpires is the noun; ask what they will do, student says officiate.

cards.sentence: We climbed over the angular rocks at the beach.
cards.notes:
1. READ: "Read the card with me." CHORAL: "-ar means relating to. We climbed over the angular rocks at the beach."
2. ASK: "What job does angular do in this sentence: noun, verb or adjective?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: adjective.
SCAN: split or wrong chorus -> do not click. Ask "What sort of rocks are they?", then re-ask on three.
3. REVEAL after the choral answer. SAY: "Angular describes the rocks, so it is an adjective. -ar means relating to, so -ar words often describe."
TRAP: noun, because rocks are things. Fix: rocks is the noun; ask what sort of rocks, student says angular.

2. SHOW the word. Students copy it correctly underneath.
3. COVER both. Students write it from memory, then tick or fix.
Say it: kam-PAYN, two beats. The g is silent, like in sign.

2. SHOW the word. Students copy it correctly underneath.

new.notes:
Why learned: it starts with question, spelled the usual way. Then the n doubles, and the French ending aire says /air/, like in millionaire.
Say it: KWES-chuh-NAIR, three beats, the last strongest.
1. COPY it twice, saying the letter names: q - u - e - s - t - i - o - n - n - a - i - r - e.
2. COVER both and write it a third time from memory, then tick or fix.
Link: a questionnaire is a list of questions you ask lots of people. In maths, you can turn its answers into percentages.

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: A complex sentence has a main clause (M) that stands alone and a subordinate clause (S) that leaves you waiting. The trigger word (T) is what makes S wait.
WHY THIS WEEK: in a persuasive piece the opinion is the M and the reason is the S. Students who can find M, S and T stop leaving a reason on its own as half a sentence.
TIME: 5 minutes, no more - I do 1 min, We do 1 question, You do 3 questions at about 30 seconds each. One question per slide; your click reveals the answer.
ROUTINE: all grammar is written in the OG book. No boards - books, fingers and voices only.
CHECK: the class met M, S and T in Term 3. Cover one half and read the other: if it leaves you waiting, it is S. A fronted S takes a comma.

i_do.title: Find M, S and T
i_do.rule: M stands alone. S leaves you waiting. T makes S wait.
i_do.example:
We should start a litter campaign
because our yard is a mess.
items: Trigger words: because, although, when, if, until, since
Cover one half. Read the other. Does it leave you waiting?
i_do.footer: Your turn: find the trigger word
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: M = We should start a litter campaign. S = because our yard is a mess. T = because.
1. SAY: "Your opinion is the half that stands alone, and your reason is the half that waits. Finding them stops you leaving a reason on its own."
2. WRITE: copy the sentence on the class board. COVER the second half and read "We should start a litter campaign". It stands alone, so write M under it.
3. WRITE: cover the first half and read "because our yard is a mess". It leaves you waiting, so write S under it. CIRCLE because and write T above it.
4. ASK: "Cover because. Does our yard is a mess stand alone now? Thumbs up or down, voices off." 5 sec. EXPECT: thumbs up - because is what made it wait.
TRAP: calling the longer half M. Fix: cover and read each half, hear which one waits, student re-labels it.
CLARIFY: if a student asks whether S always comes second, say no - S can come first, and then a comma goes where it ends.
---
PREP: a subordinating conjunction (because, although, when, if, until, since) makes its clause dependent; and, but and so are not trigger words.

we_do.title: Which word is T?
we_do.rule: T is the trigger word at the front of S.

round.prompt:
Although the questionnaire was long,
most students finished it.
round.why: it makes the first half wait
round.notes:
ANSWER: 1 - Although. It makes the first half wait.
1. SAY: "This time S comes first. Read it in your head and find the word that makes the first half wait."
2. ASK: "One finger Although, two questionnaire, three finished, voices off, show me on three." 5 sec. EXPECT: one finger.
3. REVEAL after fingers are scanned. ASK: "How do you know?" Cold call one student. EXPECT: cover Although and the rest of that half stands alone.
TRAP: choosing 3, because finished is the doing word. Fix: T is a joining word, not the verb; cover Although and read again, student votes again.
CLARIFY: if a student asks about the comma, say a fronted S takes a comma where it ends, so the reader knows where M starts.

you_do.title: Write T, then M or S
you_do.rule: Write T. Then write M or S for the first half.
you_do.footer: Check: cover T - does the rest stand alone?

round.prompt:
Our stall made a profit
because the posters attracted shoppers.
round.notes:
ANSWER: because, M.
1. SAY: "Write the trigger word, T. Then write M or S for the first half. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> cover the second half and ask which half waits, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Our stall made a profit stands alone, so it is M. Because makes the second half wait."
TRAP: writing attracted, the tract word. Fix: that is the doing word inside S; cover because and read, student writes because.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one complex sentence with a tract word in M and a different one in S. Label M, S and T.
HELP: give the trigger word list - because, although, when, if, until - and ask which one is in the sentence.

round.prompt:
When we subtract 25% from $40,
the price drops to $30.
round.why: the first half waits, so a comma ends it
round.notes:
ANSWER: When, S.
1. SAY: "Write T, then M or S for the first half. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> read the first half aloud and stop, so they hear the wait, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. When we subtract 25% from $40 leaves you waiting, so it is S. The comma shows where S ends."
TRAP: writing M because the first half is longer. Fix: cover the second half and read the first; it waits, student writes S.

round.prompt:
The polar bear swam and swam
until it reached the sea ice.
round.why: the polar bear swam and swam stands alone
round.notes:
ANSWER: until, M.
1. SAY: "Last one. Write T, then M or S for the first half. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> cover until and read it reached the sea ice, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. The first half stands alone, so it is M. Until makes the second half wait, and and just joins swam and swam."
4. SAY: "In your persuasive piece, check each reason. If it starts with because and stands on its own, join it to its M."
TRAP: writing and. Fix: and is not a trigger word - cover it and nothing waits; student writes until.
---
ANSWERS: 1. because, M  2. When, S  3. until, M. EXTENSION: e.g. Our stall will attract shoppers (M) if nothing distracts them (S); T = if.
